text:
alex: Quick question — team wants to bring up a new candidate for eval: monarch-8b-lite. Model card links to a CC-BY-NC-4.0 license and there is an additional line that says 'no redistribution of trained weights or derivatives'. Can we host this on Redwood Hosted/Dedicated or run our quantization/bench here?

maria: Heads up — CC-BY-NC is non-commercial, so Hosted API (paid, customer-facing) is usually a no-go. The extra 'no redistribution' clause is pretty restrictive. Can you paste the exact snippet? :eyes:

alex: Paste from the model card: "The model weights are provided for non-commercial research and evaluation only. Redistribution of the model weights, including quantized or otherwise modified binary files, is prohibited without express permission."

ravi: Understood. So two questions for infra/legal: 1) Is running int8 quantization locally on Redwood infra allowed if we don't publish the quantized files? 2) If a customer brings the weights and asks us to run benchmarks in Dedicated, are we allowed to host them?

sarah: Operational view: Even if we run it in Dedicated, we're still providing a hosted service. Hosting third-party NC models on our Hosted/Dedicated product for paying customers looks like commercial use to me. Private/on-prem where the customer deploys inside their VPC might be a different story.

maria: Legal summary: (a) CC-BY-NC prohibits commercial exploitation — hosting for paying customers qualifies as commercial. (b) The explicit 'no redistribution' clause likely covers quantized derivatives. That means we cannot create or transfer quantized weight files outside of the licensee's environment. (c) If a customer brings the weights and keeps them behind their boundary (Private/on-prem), we can operate on them under a contract that requires them to confirm they have rights.

josh: For product context — team wanted a quick POC on Hosted to show perf numbers. Sounds like we need to avoid that path. Could we do a controlled internal bench and only publish metrics?

ravi: We can run local bench jobs that never persist quantized binaries: use ephemeral instances, do in-memory quantization and immediately bench and delete. Avoid uploading artifacts to shared buckets. Publish results/metrics but not the quantized files.

maria: That's acceptable as a temporary evaluation *for internal research* provided we don't generate redistributable artifacts. Still recommend asking upstream for explicit permission if we want to use it beyond internal tests or if results feed a customer-facing feature.

license-bot: license-check: CC-BY-NC-4.0 + custom "no redistribution" clause detected. Status: FLAGGED. Recommended action: escalate to Legal (maria) and do not upload derivative weights to shared storage.

alex: One more: attribution. CC-BY requires attribution when distributing the work, but what about generated outputs (responses)? The model card mentions attribution in UI for any public demos. Do we need to show a banner or add text in TOS?

maria: Attribution usually applies to the model files, but licensors sometimes add UX requirements for outputs. If the model card explicitly asks for UI attribution for demos, we should comply for any public-facing demo. For internal evals or research reports, include a footnote: "Model: Monarch-8b-lite (CC-BY-NC-4.0)". For hosted product use — not allowed anyway without commercial license.

ravi: Practical checklist for the team to run evals now:
- run quantization only on ephemeral instances
- do not write quantized .bin files to long-term buckets
- log hyperparams & perf metrics only (OK to publish)
- if customer provides weights, require written attestation of licensing + sign-off from Legal before running in Dedicated

sarah: Operational addition: create a disposable workspace script to wipe volumes after run, and add an automated verify-delete step to CI that ensures no binary remains. I can help with a helper script.

alex: OK I'll open a Legal ticket and mark the onboarding row "license: blocked - NC/no-redistrib" in the tracker. I'll also tag the bench as internal-only and follow the ephemeral workflow.

maria: Sounds good. I'll draft an email template we can send to the model authors requesting a commercial license or permission to redistribute quantized derivatives. If they grant it, we can re-evaluate hosting options. cc @legal-team

josh: Thanks. Also: if we get written permission, we should make sure the commercial license explicitly covers: redistribution of quantized weights, serving from Hosted/Dedicated, and attribution terms.

alex: Filing ticket now: https://redwood.internal/triage/12481 — assigning to @maria and @ravi. I'll update tracker when we get a reply from upstream. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — marking this thread as "hold" in onboarding board.

ravi: Will proceed with local ephemeral bench this afternoon and share numbers here (no artifacts).

alex: Great — keep it short and paste methodology so Legal can review the risk.

sarah: I'll put together the wipe script and share before the run.

license-bot: ticket-linked: https://redwood.internal/triage/12481. Reminder: DO NOT persist any derivative weights to shared storage.
